column1: # aontu:code -- THE OUTPUT VOCABULARY (docs/capability-review/
# g9-transformation.md §1 with the fragment algebra of its second
# amendment; docs/design/RENDER.0.md D2 and P1). An aontu transform
# evaluates to an instance of this schema, and `aontu render` turns the
# instance into bytes; because it is an ordinary schema, a transform's
# result is checked by unification before anything is rendered.
# Columns: name<TAB>mode<TAB>src<TAB>expect
# The source is BUNDLED with the engine (the aontu/ tree, ADR-036) and
# served under the aontu: scheme (aontu-scheme.tsv). The two copies are
# the same bytes: `shapes-hash` below hashes a document that references
# every alias, so the bodies are pinned in both engines and cannot
# drift without a red suite. THE ROOT IS NOT type()-MARKED, on purpose:
# `render` reads the instance through generate(), and a type()-marked
# subtree does not generate (VERIFIED, both ports) -- so a document that
# includes the vocabulary and writes no units generates `code: {units:
# []}`, which is what it said.
# EXPERIMENTAL until the distribution layer can version it by
# canon-hash.
# THE PIN MOVED ON 2026-09-07, and what moved it is the point of it.
# Every shape here is a close()-marked alias used as a SPREAD TEMPLATE,
# and the hash form was dropping the close() at every one of them
# (use-cases/BUGS.md §60): 139 close() wrappers where the fixed form
# has 592. So this row pinned the shapes with their CLOSEDNESS ERASED
# -- a vocabulary edited from close({...}) to {...} anywhere would have
# left it green, which is the one thing it exists to catch.
# Every expectation was obtained by running BOTH engines and diffing.
vocabulary-is-served
column3: @"aontu:code"\nx: 1

column1: shapes-hash
column3: @"aontu:code"\nshapes: { unit: %unit, decl: %decl, type: %type, check: %check, piece: %piece, field: %field, source: %source }

column1: # A UNIT: a path, a language, its declarations; an inline profile
# override rides on it (RENDER.0.md D4, D5).
unit-minimal
column3: @"aontu:code"\naontu: Code: units: [{ path: "a.txt", lang: "text", decls: [] }]

column1: unit-profile-inline
column3: @"aontu:code"\naontu: Code: units: [{ path: "a", lang: "text", decls: [], profile: { indent: { width: 4 } } }]

column1: unit-unknown-key-refused
column3: @"aontu:code"\naontu: Code: units: [{ path: "a", lang: "text", decls: [], module: "m" }]

column1: unit-lang-empty-refused
column3: @"aontu:code"\naontu: Code: units: [{ path: "a", lang: "", decls: [] }]

column1: # THE FRAGMENT ALGEBRA is flat: a line at a depth, a blank, a raw; a
# bare string is a line at depth 0. No inline piece holds a line
# terminator -- the renderer's totality invariant, checked HERE, at the
# node, before any renderer runs.
frag-valid
column3: @"aontu:code"\naontu: Code: units: [{ path: "a.py", lang: "python", decls: [{ k: "frag", of: ["class Planet:", { k: "line", at: 1, of: ["name = ", { k: "ref", name: "Name" }] }, { k: "blank" }, { k: "raw", at: 1, text: "def f():\\n    pass", reindent: false }] }] }]

column1: frag-string-newline-refused
column3: @"aontu:code"\naontu: Code: units: [{ path: "a", lang: "text", decls: [{ k: "frag", of: ["ok", "bad\\nline"] }] }]

column1: frag-inline-newline-refused
column3: @"aontu:code"\naontu: Code: units: [{ path: "a", lang: "text", decls: [{ k: "frag", of: [{ k: "line", of: ["bad\\nline"] }] }] }]

column1: frag-at-negative-refused
column3: @"aontu:code"\naontu: Code: units: [{ path: "a", lang: "text", decls: [{ k: "frag", of: [{ k: "line", at: -1, of: ["x"] }] }] }]

column1: frag-at-over-bound-refused
column3: @"aontu:code"\naontu: Code: units: [{ path: "a", lang: "text", decls: [{ k: "frag", of: [{ k: "line", at: 65, of: ["x"] }] }] }]

column1: frag-blank-zero-refused
column3: @"aontu:code"\naontu: Code: units: [{ path: "a", lang: "text", decls: [{ k: "frag", of: [{ k: "blank", n: 0 }] }] }]

column1: # THE DECLARATIONS, and the spelling rules the design found by probe.
record-valid
column3: @"aontu:code"\naontu: Code: units: [{ path: "ts/domain.ts", lang: "typescript", decls: [{ k: "record", name: "Customer", fields: [{ name: "id", type: { k: "prim", prim: "string" } }, { name: "email", type: { k: "prim", prim: "string" }, optional: true }] }] }]

column1: text-escape
column3: @"aontu:code"\naontu: Code: units: [{ path: "a.rb", lang: "ruby", decls: [{ k: "text", lang: "ruby", text: "puts 1" }] }]

column1: # Rule 1: an atom kind in an instance must be QUOTED. `prim: string` is
# the kind, not the string "string", and it cannot generate.
prim-unquoted-refused
column3: @"aontu:code"\naontu: Code: units: [{ path: "a", lang: "text", decls: [{ k: "alias", name: "T", type: { k: "prim", prim: string } }] }]

column1: prim-unknown-refused
column3: @"aontu:code"\naontu: Code: units: [{ path: "a", lang: "text", decls: [{ k: "alias", name: "T", type: { k: "prim", prim: "int32" } }] }]

column1: name-not-an-identifier-refused
column3: @"aontu:code"\naontu: Code: units: [{ path: "a", lang: "text", decls: [{ k: "alias", name: "9x", type: { k: "prim", prim: "int" } }] }]

column1: field-unknown-key-refused
column3: @"aontu:code"\naontu: Code: units: [{ path: "a", lang: "text", decls: [{ k: "record", name: "R", fields: [{ name: "id", type: { k: "prim", prim: "string" }, nullable: true }] }] }]

column1: source-hash-not-a-pin-refused
column3: @"aontu:code"\naontu: Code: { source: { hash: "sha256-abc" }, units: [] }

column1: # CONTAINER TYPES TAKE LEAVES ONLY. Both engines refuse the nested
# list at the declaration; the CODES differ (TypeScript `|:trial-nil`,
# Go `empty` -- use-cases/BUGS.md §80), so the row pins the path.
container-nested-refused
column3: @"aontu:code"\naontu: Code: units: [{ path: "a", lang: "text", decls: [{ k: "alias", name: "T", type: { k: "list", of: { k: "list", of: { k: "prim", prim: "int" } } } }] }]
